notes: Each entry is a top-level key next to _schema. Ignore keys that start with _ when reading.
Create entries only for successfully imported components with available code; a blocked diagnosis is never a mapping.
Use <FILE_KEY>:<COMPONENT_OR_SET_NODE_ID> as the default entry key. For remotes without a reliable file/node id, use componentKey:<COMPONENT_KEY>.
The entry key is an identifier; include that same ref in figma.refs.

Use <FILE_KEY>:<NODE_ID> with the file key of the file where the node lives (the DS file for local nodes; the library's file key for a remote component when the tool returns it) and componentKey:<KEY> whenever the tool returns a component key.

Resolve components by matching a stable ref against figma.refs or any figma.variants[*].refs. A variant ref match identifies the matched variant and its props. Do not use the placed instance id as a stable mapping.
A ref can belong to only one entry, and all refs from the same Figma node/instance must resolve to the same entry. If not, report a conflict.
When updating a component, merge newly discovered refs into existing refs arrays instead of replacing them.
